knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 1.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly defines reproducible research and names required elements?
knowledge_checks.body: Select reproducibility meaning and element list.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Reconstruction from shared artefacts is the core. One local rerun, memory, or papers-only scope misstates reproducibility.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Others can reconstruct results; data, code, documentation required.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: One-off rerun, memory-only, or excluding internal analyses.

choices.label: Reproducible research lets others (or a future you) reconstruct the same analysis results from stated inputs and steps. Required elements include versioned or clearly identified data, scripted code paths, and documented environment and decisions.
Reproducibility means re-running one notebook cell once on a local laptop; shared data, code, and documentation are optional.
An analysis is reproducible if the author remembers the steps; formal versioning and scripts are bureaucracy only.
Reproducibility applies only to published papers, not to internal pricing or reserves work.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 1.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A colleague says their pricing analysis is reproducible because they can re-run one notebook cell on their laptop. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Define reproducibility; name elements; refuse one-off rerun claim.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Shared data, code, and environment documentation enable reconstruction. Duplicate local output, email notes, or dated filenames alone fail.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Reconstruct from shared artefacts; refuse one-off rerun.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating reproducibility with a single local re-run or weak versioning.

choices.label: Reproducible research means others can reconstruct the same results from stated inputs and steps. Examples of required elements: versioned data or clear extract identity, scripted code, documented environment/parameters. A one-off local re-run without shared artefacts is not reproducibility.
Re-running the last cell proves reproducibility because the output appeared twice on the same machine.
Documentation is unnecessary if the colleague wrote detailed comments in email about what they did.
Reproducibility is satisfied when the notebook filename includes the analysis date; data versioning is optional.

worked_example.title: Judge whether a one-cell notebook rerun is reproducible
worked_example.problem_statement: A colleague says their pricing analysis is reproducible because they can re-run one notebook cell on their laptop. Decide whether that claim meets the definition of reproducible research, and name required elements that are still missing.

given.value: re-run one notebook cell on their laptop
others can reconstruct the same results from stated inputs and steps

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Compare the colleague's evidence with the reconstruct-from-shared-artefacts standard before judging.

steps.label: State the reproducibility standard
steps.attempt_cue: Define reproducible research in one sentence.
steps.explanation: Reproducible research lets others (or a future you) reconstruct the same analysis results from stated inputs and steps.
steps.calculation: Standard = reconstruct same results from stated inputs/steps

steps.label: List required elements
steps.attempt_cue: Name data, code, and environment/documentation pieces.
steps.explanation: Required elements include versioned or clearly identified data, scripted code paths, and documented environment and decisions (including parameters/seeds where relevant).
steps.calculation: Need: versioned/identified data + scripted code + documented environment/decisions

steps.label: Judge the colleague claim
steps.attempt_cue: Decide pass/fail and name what a one-cell local rerun lacks.
steps.explanation: A one-off local re-run without shared artefacts does not let others reconstruct the analysis. The claim fails the reproducibility standard.
steps.calculation: Judgment: FAIL; missing shared data identity, full scripted path, and environment docs
steps.result: Not reproducible under the reconstruction standard

worked_example.final_answer: Not reproducible: a one-off local notebook-cell rerun lacks shared versioned data, scripted end-to-end code, and documented environment/decisions that others can use to reconstruct the results.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Equating 'I can re-run this cell on my laptop' with reproducibility, without requiring shared artefacts that let someone else reconstruct the same results.
